ledgerFoodIntakeAndPopulation.note: In the ledger one part creatures eat less in most arms, including SEG_MOVE alone where the garden shows the gap closing: an observational gap reflects who carries parts as well as what parts do. Populations grow from about 190 to 270 with movement freed and to 385 to 455 with two or three penalties removed.

interpretation: The body cost is caused by the part. Given to one of three otherwise identical newborns released side by side, a bare part cuts lifetime offspring by 52.2 percent (49.2 to 55.9), more than the ledger's 40.3, whose one part creatures often carry fins that offset the thrust penalty.

Almost all of it is the movement penalty. Freeing movement alone takes the cost to 2.4 percent in the ledger (-1.7 to 5.9) and 6.1 in the garden (-1.9 to 13.4). Its Shapley share of the all-off cost is 0.95 in the ledger and 1.01 in the garden; the threshold's is 0.49 and 0.45, metabolism's 0.44 and 0.57. Each interval lies above zero.

The penalty works through food (exploratory). In the garden a bare part founder eats 30 percent less algae than its identical siblings; with movement freed it eats 8 percent more. A part divides paddle thrust by 1.2, so a finless body swims at five sixths speed, turns 11 percent slower and is pushed less by the current, in a dish where 69 percent of control founders die starving.

The shares sum to about two because the three costs overlap: remove any two and the part costs nothing or pays, remove all three and it becomes an advantage of 35 percent in the ledger and 54 in the garden. What a part still does then is store 45 percent more energy, and where most creatures starve a bigger store is worth that much.
For the 65 percent v1.43 left unexplained: with the threshold switch on, freeing movement removes 171 percent of what remains and freeing metabolism 108 percent, each more than enough alone.

Remove the penalties and bodies take over (descriptive). Bodied share of the living population rises from 14 percent to 70 with movement freed, 83 with the threshold and metabolism freed, and 99 with all three off, where bodies average 5.5 parts against a cap of 6.

Two of four predictions failed, both about movement. I expected metabolism to outweigh movement and movement's share to stay under 0.15, reasoning that a slower body also burns less. Foraging lost to slowness is far larger than burn saved.

This is selection, not drift, favouring more body structure: at a mean population of 423 the advantage of a part in the all-off arm has intervals far from zero in both instruments. But what selection favours there is storage, a side effect of how capacity is computed, not anything a part does with its organs. It is not yet the target this line of work is after.
toolingFaults: The Browser pane closed seconds after the first launch began and took all eight tabs with it. No run had finished and only tab A's start had been recorded. The tabs were relaunched one at a time, from the same committed build, behind a static page; every preflight passed again.

Background tabs got about half a CPU core each, and runs with movement freed or with two or more penalties removed took 1.6 to 2.7 times as long as the defaults, because their populations were larger and carried more parts. The study took 176 minutes across eight tabs.
macOS has no timeout command, so the first watcher never started; it was rerun without one.
honestLimitations: SEG_MOVE bundles three effects, thrust, turning and the current's push; which of them carries the cost is not known.
The garden's part is bare. Parts that evolve carry fins, spikes and shells, which is one reason the ledger cost is lower.
Six seeds per arm. Percentile bootstrap intervals over six units tend to be somewhat narrow.
The garden null interval excluded zero in one of eight arms (SEG_MOVE + SEG_BURN, -9.6 percent), exploratory.
The effects interact strongly, so Shapley shares are averages over the orders in which switches are removed, not independent parts.
One machine; cross machine determinism is known broken.
